title: Six wins in a row
situation: You have won 6 [[demo-account|demo]] trades in a row. You feel you have figured the market out. You are thinking of skipping your pre-trade checklist and risking three times your usual amount on the next trade.
question: What do you do next?

responses.text: Go ahead. Six wins show the method works.
responses.explanation: Six trades is a very small sample, and a run of wins can happen by chance. Tripling risk makes the next loss three times as big.

responses.text: Use the bigger size, but still do the checklist.
responses.explanation: Keeping the checklist is good. Changing size because of a streak, rather than a planned rule, is still a reaction.

responses.text: Keep your usual size and checklist, and review the 6 trades to see whether each one followed your rules.
responses.explanation: This checks whether the wins came from your process or from luck. Your risk stays where you set it when calm.

takeaway: A winning streak is a reason to check your process, not to loosen it.
